overview.text: Today's developments center on advancing agent capabilities, memory systems, and efficient architectures. Scaling data and model capacity improves embodied learning in diverse virtual worlds, while new approaches address the security risks of training computer-use agents directly in the wild through environment synthesis. To overcome context and weight limitations during long-term deployment, memory-centric continual learning frameworks enable sustained adaptation for autonomous foundation model agents. In parallel, research into linear-attention language models introduces periodic and channel-aligned encoding of four-bit recurrent states to reduce memory overhead and increase accelerator sharing. Finally, open releases like Spark-X2.6-4B and specialized coding models continue to push the frontier for local and specialized agent architectures.

entries.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
entries.summary: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws.
entries.why: Scaling data, diversity, and model capacity improves embodied learning across diverse virtual worlds.

entries.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
entries.summary: Agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world. However, scaling such learning directly in real-world computer systems is challenging and can introduce substantial security risks.
entries.why: Synthetic environments allow computer-use agents to learn safely without facing direct real-world security risks.

entries.title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
entries.summary: Autonomous agents powered by foundation models can reason, plan, and use tools, but their fixed weights and context limits hinder sustained learning from experience over long-term deployment.
entries.why: Memory-centric continual learning helps autonomous agents overcome fixed weight limits during long-term deployment.

entries.title: TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking
entries.summary: Using an LLM to generate training data for another is among the most general ways to train one, and it remains common practice.
entries.why: Distilling models using self-generated thinking traces remains a core practice for training efficient systems.

entries.title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
entries.summary: Linear-attention language models keep their context in a recurrent state of fixed size, where an inference system stores one copy of this state for every sequence it decodes at the same time. Storing the state at lower precision therefore lets more sequences share an accelerator.
entries.why: Four-bit recurrent state encoding allows more sequences to share an accelerator efficiently in linear-attention models.

entries.title: Building AI Research Teams for Autonomous Discovery of Linear Attention Architectures
entries.summary: Autonomous agents can increasingly propose ideas, modify code, and run experiments, creating an opportunity to accelerate scientific discovery using teams of collaborative AI researchers.
entries.why: Autonomous AI research teams can propose ideas and run experiments to accelerate architecture discovery.

entries.title: SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience
entries.summary: Spatial reasoning requires more than access to geometric tools: a reasoner must decide when direct observation is sufficient and when to reconstruct, measure, or change reference frames.
entries.why: Spatial intelligence requires reasoners to dynamically decide when to use direct observation or reference frames.
